# Client configuration reference

Every server, with the credentials it needs and a ready config for Claude Code and Codex. Start with [Connect your AI client](connect-clients.md) for the walkthrough.

Snippets read secrets from your shell environment (`${VAR}` in Claude Code, `env_vars` in Codex), so no secret is written into a config file. Optional variables are in the tables but left out of the snippets.

| Server                                                                               | Config name           | Port |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- | ---- |
| [Bid Manager MCP Server](#bid-manager-mcp-server-cesteral-dbm)                       | `cesteral-dbm`        | 3001 |
| [DV360 MCP Server](#dv360-mcp-server-cesteral-dv360)                                 | `cesteral-dv360`      | 3002 |
| [The Trade Desk MCP Server](#the-trade-desk-mcp-server-cesteral-ttd)                 | `cesteral-ttd`        | 3003 |
| [Google Ads MCP Server](#google-ads-mcp-server-cesteral-gads)                        | `cesteral-gads`       | 3004 |
| [Meta Ads MCP Server](#meta-ads-mcp-server-cesteral-meta)                            | `cesteral-meta`       | 3005 |
| [LinkedIn Ads MCP Server](#linkedin-ads-mcp-server-cesteral-linkedin)                | `cesteral-linkedin`   | 3006 |
| [TikTok Ads MCP Server](#tiktok-ads-mcp-server-cesteral-tiktok)                      | `cesteral-tiktok`     | 3007 |
| [Campaign Manager 360 MCP Server](#campaign-manager-360-mcp-server-cesteral-cm360)   | `cesteral-cm360`      | 3008 |
| [Snapchat Ads MCP Server](#snapchat-ads-mcp-server-cesteral-snapchat)                | `cesteral-snapchat`   | 3009 |
| [Search Ads 360 MCP Server](#search-ads-360-mcp-server-cesteral-sa360)               | `cesteral-sa360`      | 3010 |
| [Pinterest Ads MCP Server](#pinterest-ads-mcp-server-cesteral-pinterest)             | `cesteral-pinterest`  | 3011 |
| [Amazon DSP MCP Server](#amazon-dsp-mcp-server-cesteral-amazon-dsp)                  | `cesteral-amazon-dsp` | 3012 |
| [Microsoft Advertising MCP Server](#microsoft-advertising-mcp-server-cesteral-msads) | `cesteral-msads`      | 3013 |

## Bid Manager MCP Server (cesteral-dbm)

Bid Manager reporting and query workflows for DV360 campaign performance analysis. Port `3001`.

### Credentials (stdio)

| Variable               | Needed                              | Secret | What it is                                                         |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE` | one of: service-account (preferred) | no     | Path to a Google service account JSON key with Bid Manager access. |
| `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` | one of: service-account             | yes    | The service account JSON itself, instead of a file path.           |

### Claude Code, stdio

Put this in `.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cesteral-dbm": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@cesteral/dbm-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "MCP_TRANSPORT_MODE": "stdio",
        "SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE": "${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Or add it from the shell:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio cesteral-dbm --env MCP_TRANSPORT_MODE=stdio --env SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE="$SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE" -- npx -y @cesteral/dbm-mcp
```

### Codex, stdio

Put this in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.cesteral-dbm]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@cesteral/dbm-mcp"]
env = { MCP_TRANSPORT_MODE = "stdio" }
env_vars = ["SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE"]
```

### Self-hosted HTTP

Run `./scripts/dev-server.sh dbm-mcp` first. Headers the server reads:

| Header                          | Needed   | Value                      | What it is                                                              |
| ------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `X-Cesteral-Google-Auth-Type`   | required | `service_account`          | Credential type.                                                        |
| `X-Cesteral-Google-Credentials` | required | `$DBM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_B64` | Service account JSON, base64-encoded (base64 < key.json \| tr -d '\n'). |

Claude Code:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cesteral-dbm": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:3001/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-Cesteral-Google-Auth-Type": "service_account",
        "X-Cesteral-Google-Credentials": "${DBM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_B64}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Codex: this server needs more than one header, which Codex's `bearer_token_env_var` cannot carry. Use the stdio config above.

## Google Ads MCP Server (cesteral-gads)

Google Ads management — campaign writes, GAQL reporting, bulk mutate, validation, and previews. Port `3004`.

### Credentials (stdio)

| Variable                 | Needed   | Secret | What it is                                |
| ------------------------ | -------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `GADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN`   | required | yes    | Google Ads developer token.               |
| `GADS_CLIENT_ID`         | required | no     | OAuth2 client ID.                         |
| `GADS_CLIENT_SECRET`     | required | yes    | OAuth2 client secret.                     |
| `GADS_REFRESH_TOKEN`     | required | yes    | OAuth2 refresh token.                     |
| `GADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID` | optional | no     | Manager account customer ID, digits only. |

### Claude Code, stdio

Put this in `.mcp.json`:

```json

  "mcpServers": {
    "cesteral-gads": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@cesteral/gads-mcp"],

        "GADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN": "${GADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN}",
        "GADS_CLIENT_ID": "${GADS_CLIENT_ID}",
        "GADS_CLIENT_SECRET": "${GADS_CLIENT_SECRET}",
        "GADS_REFRESH_TOKEN": "${GADS_REFRESH_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Or add it from the shell:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio cesteral-gads --env MCP_TRANSPORT_MODE=stdio --env GADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN="$GADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN" --env GADS_CLIENT_ID="$GADS_CLIENT_ID" --env GADS_CLIENT_SECRET="$GADS_CLIENT_SECRET" --env GADS_REFRESH_TOKEN="$GADS_REFRESH_TOKEN" -- npx -y @cesteral/gads-mcp

command = "npx"

```

### Self-hosted HTTP

Run `./scripts/dev-server.sh gads-mcp` first. Headers the server reads:

| Header                     | Needed   | Value                     | What it is                   |
| -------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `X-Gads-Developer-Token`   | required | `$GADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN`   | Google Ads developer token.  |
| `X-Gads-Client-Id`         | required | `$GADS_CLIENT_ID`         | OAuth2 client ID.            |
| `X-Gads-Client-Secret`     | required | `$GADS_CLIENT_SECRET`     | OAuth2 client secret.        |
| `X-Gads-Refresh-Token`     | required | `$GADS_REFRESH_TOKEN`     | OAuth2 refresh token.        |
| `X-Gads-Login-Customer-Id` | optional | `$GADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID` | Manager account customer ID. |
